security_audit.summary: Review confirmed eight findings covering compile-time environment-file loading and an automated release example that deletes output and publishes to npm. The remaining 158 detections are documentation, template literals, fixed local operations, or public links without malicious behavior. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or concealed execution was found.

remediation.issue: The release example runs destructive cleanup and npm publication without a confirmation boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell cleanup with validated fs.rm calls. Move npm publish behind an explicit confirmation or dry-run step.

remediation.issue: Environment-file examples can embed sensitive production values into distributable bundles.
remediation.suggestion: Use narrow prefixes and document secret exclusions. Inspect generated output before publication and keep environment files outside package artifacts.

remediation.issue: The watch example enables shell execution for a command that does not require it.
remediation.suggestion: Set shell to false and retain the fixed argument array to reduce command interpretation risk.

content.value_statement: Library builds often need multiple formats, declarations, and package validation. This skill guides tsdown configuration, migration, framework integration, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Configure library entries, output formats, targets, source maps, cleaning, and dependency externalization.
Generate TypeScript declarations and package exports for publishable libraries.
Migrate common tsup settings and identify options that need manual changes.
Configure React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, CSS, WebAssembly, and executable builds.
Explain programmatic builds, hooks, watch mode, workspaces, and CI validation.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and does not bundle projects unless commands are explicitly executed.
tsdown requires Node.js 22.18.0 or newer for build execution.
CSS and executable features require separate experimental packages and platform testing.
Generated configurations still require tests against each supported runtime and package manager.

use_cases.title: Publish a TypeScript library
use_cases.description: Create ESM and CommonJS outputs, declarations, exports, and validation settings for an npm package.

use_cases.title: Migrate from tsup
use_cases.description: Translate existing build settings to tsdown and identify incompatible or renamed options.

use_cases.title: Standardize monorepo builds
use_cases.description: Define shared workspace builds, framework plugins, dependency rules, and CI checks across packages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic library build
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tsdown configuration for [entry file]. Output ESM and CommonJS, generate declarations, and clean only the distribution directory.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a new TypeScript library with one entry point.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a tsup configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this tsup configuration to tsdown: [configuration]. Preserve entries, formats, declarations, externals, and source maps. Explain unsupported options.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when replacing tsup without changing package behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a component library
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure tsdown for a [framework] component library. Externalize framework peers, generate declarations, and include the required compiler plugin.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for React, Vue, Solid, or Svelte packages.

prompt_templates.title: Design a guarded release build
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monorepo build for [packages]. Add workspace filters, CI validation, output checks, and a publication step requiring explicit confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced release automation across multiple packages.

output_examples.input: Bundle a TypeScript library for Node.js and browser consumers.
output: Recommended build: ESM and CommonJS outputs, declarations, source maps, and a clean distribution directory.
Dependency plan: externalize declared peers and test both runtime targets before publication.

output_examples.input: Migrate an existing tsup build with multiple entries.
output: Migration summary: preserve entry patterns, formats, declaration generation, and external dependencies.
Review list: verify renamed options, output extensions, cleaning behavior, and package exports.

output_examples.input: Improve slow rebuilds in a component library.
output_examples.output: Use watch exclusions for dependencies, build output, repository metadata, and tests. Consider disabling declaration generation during local watch sessions.

best_practices: Inspect the existing package manifest, runtime targets, and peer dependencies before creating a configuration.
Keep output in a dedicated directory and validate the resolved path before cleaning.
Test packed artifacts on every supported runtime before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not set the output directory to the project root while cleaning is enabled.
Do not bundle framework peer dependencies unless consumers require embedded copies.
Do not load secret environment values into compile-time definitions.

faq.question: Does this skill install or run tsdown automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Package installation and build commands run only when the user or agent executes them.

faq.question: Which Node.js version is required?
faq.answer: tsdown requires Node.js 22.18.0 or newer to build. Generated packages can target older Node.js versions.

faq.question: Can it migrate a tsup configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps common settings and identifies options that require manual adjustment.

faq.question: Does it support component libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover React, Vue, Solid, and Svelte integration patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate TypeScript declarations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers declaration generation, declaration source maps, compiler options, and framework-specific settings.

faq.question: How should environment values be handled?
faq.answer: Use explicit prefixes, exclude secrets, keep environment files unpublished, and inspect generated bundles for embedded values.
